nextGame.blurb: Jeremiah Smith scored on his first two touches and Julian Sayin threw four touchdown passes in No. 5 Ohio State's 45-16 win over Maryland. It was messier than the score suggests — two turnovers and eight penalties, including a 52-yard Daniel Wingate pick-six — and Ryan Day said as much with a trip to Indiana and games against USC and Oregon looming.

Ten turnovers, seven by Oregon, defined a messy afternoon in Eugene, and No. 21 UCLA survived it 17-15 to stay unbeaten. Wayne Knight ran for 103 yards and a score and caught a 9-yard touchdown from backup Ty Dieffenbach after Nico Iamaleava left with a lower-leg injury; the Bruins then stuffed Jordon Davison on a second try at a two-point conversion and watched the Ducks fumble away their final possession.

bubbleNote.blurb: Oregon moved up two spots to the 14 seed, two away from the field, and its next test comes against a No. 21 opponent — no margin for another sloppy afternoon.

nextGame.blurb: Dwight Phillips Jr. churned out 120 yards and Georgia piled up 206 on the ground without leading rusher Nate Frazier, grinding out a 20-17 win in Tuscaloosa. Gunner Stockton accounted for both Bulldog touchdowns — a 20-yard strike to London Humphreys and a 14-yard keeper — and Peyton Woodring's 23-yard fourth-quarter field goal held up after a no-call, a JK Bolden sack and a late Alabama personal foul let Georgia bleed out the clock.

Freshman Jonaz Walton broke a 97-yard touchdown run — the third-longest offensive play in Notre Dame Stadium history — and finished with 181 yards as No. 3 Notre Dame hammered Stanford 58-7. Five Irish touchdowns covered 30 yards or more, and the win was their 16th in a row, all by double digits.

Tate Sandell's 47-yard field goal on the final snap gave Oklahoma a 27-24 upset of No. 1 Texas in the Red River rivalry. The Sooners manufactured points without their offense — Dakoda Fields fell on a blocked punt in the end zone and Peyton Bowen took an interception 42 yards to the house — and after picking off Arch Manning again with 19 seconds left, John Mateer hit two throws to set up the winner rather than play for overtime.

Down 17-6 early in the fourth, No. 7 Indiana struck twice through Nick Marsh — a 75-yard catch-and-run and then a 44-yard fourth-and-1 touchdown from Josh Hoover — to beat Nebraska 20-17. It's the Hoosiers' 22nd straight win, and it took every bit of a hard-fought road night to get it.

Jamal Roberts carried 34 times for a career-high 222 yards and two scores, including a 54-yard dagger with 2:49 left, as No. 14 Missouri handled Texas A&M 27-6. Blake Craig added field goals from 50 and 51 yards, and the Tigers' defense picked off Marcel Reed twice to keep the Aggies stuck in field-goal mode all afternoon.

No. 9 Ole Miss buried Vanderbilt 52-17, scoring on four straight first-half drives to lead 42-3 at the break. Trinidad Chambliss threw for 213 yards and three touchdowns and ran for another, and the Rebels turned four Commodore giveaways into 24 points, including Suntarine Perkins' short fumble return for a score.

Kentucky stunned No. 10 LSU 35-34 in overtime when Kenny Minchey ran in the two-point conversion untouched after C.J. Baxter's 1-yard score. The Wildcats forced the extra period on Adam Zouagui's 33-yard kick with 12 seconds left — after he'd missed from 42 and 26 — and LSU's two turnovers, including a Sam Leavitt strip-sack, loomed large despite Leavitt's 275 yards and overtime touchdown run.

Jayden Maiava threw for 301 yards and three touchdowns as No. 19 USC quieted the largest crowd in Beaver Stadium history, 31-23. The Trojans answered Penn State's only lead with King Miller's 13-yard touchdown run, and Christian Pierce's forced fumble with 3:59 left ended the Nittany Lions' night for good.

Backup Jeremy Hecklinski, starting for the injured Hank Brown, threw three touchdown passes while the Hawkeyes defense held the Huskies to minus-3 rushing yards and forced punts on their first five drives.

Even after the turnover-littered loss to UCLA, Oregon sits 13th in the poll and remains a top-10 team to the models — 8th in SP+, 9th in FPI.

fieldStorylines.blurb: The SEC's auto bid is a one-spot argument: No. 1 Texas still holds the lead with No. 2 Georgia breathing down its neck.
Ohio State at No. 5 is the Big Ten's bid-holder, but No. 7 Indiana is just two spots back — close enough that one Saturday flips it.
BYU at No. 8 leads the Big 12 race, with No. 11 Texas Tech three spots behind and plenty of league schedule left to close it.
